prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
(empty)

New part:
S001: This section defines the mission, scope, and operating roles for automated medication dispensing and medication returns in the hospital.
S002: The workflow is intended to support timely fulfillment while preserving pharmacist oversight, medication traceability, and clinical control.
S003: The concept covers order intake, pharmacy preparation and verification, ward access, and the initial handling of returned medication.
S004: In this concept, the Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot is called Cinderwake.
S005: In this concept, the Pharmacy Verification Station is called Juniper.
S006: In this concept, the Medication Return Kiosk is called Tallowmere.
S007: In this concept, the Registered Nurse is called Larkspur.
S008: The Medication Order Gateway provides the controlled entry point for medication orders and communicates order status to authorized hospital systems.
S009: The Clinical Pharmacist reviews clinical appropriateness and resolves medication questions that require professional judgment.
S010: The Pharmacy Technician performs routine preparation tasks within approved procedures and escalates discrepancies to the Clinical Pharmacist.
S011: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot produces the Priority Refill Tote Tag for eligible refill work.
S012: The Clinical Pharmacist produces the Dose Exception Review Slip when an order requires a documented exception review.
S013: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot prepares eligible medication against the active order and records its handling actions.
S014: The Pharmacy Verification Station supports a final verification step before medication is released for delivery or ward access.
S015: The Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler maintains monitored storage conditions for medication that requires temperature control.
S016: The East Tube Dispatch Console and West Tube Dispatch Console provide controlled interfaces for routing authorized pharmacy deliveries.
S017: The Pneumatic Tube Network carries compatible deliveries between designated hospital locations under established routing procedures.
S018: Ward medication access remains subject to local authorization, patient-care requirements, and applicable cabinet controls.
S019: The Charge Nurse coordinates ward readiness, communicates operational constraints, and supports escalation when dispensing service is disrupted.
S020: The Medication Return Kiosk provides a controlled point for recording medication returns and capturing return details.
S021: The Medication Return Kiosk produces the Return Bin Audit Label for a recorded return transaction.
S022: Returned medication remains segregated from usable stock until its disposition has been assessed under hospital procedure.
S023: The Hospital Courier supports authorized movement of medication and returns when automated routes are unavailable or unsuitable.
S024: The Biomedical Engineer maintains supported equipment, while the IT Operations Specialist monitors system connectivity and service availability.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response:
{"summary":"Mission/scope: Hospital automated medication dispensing and initial medication-return handling cover order intake, pharmacy preparation/verification, and ward access, supporting timely fulfillment while preserving pharmacist oversight, medication traceability, and clinical control.
Elements, actors, aliases, and responsibilities:
• Medication Order Gateway: controlled medication-order entry; communicates order status to authorized hospital systems.
• Clinical Pharmacist: reviews clinical appropriateness, resolves medication questions requiring professional judgment, and produces the Dose Exception Review Slip for orders requiring documented exception review.

• Registered Nurse (Larkspur).

• Biomedical Engineer: maintains supported equipment.
• IT Operations Specialist: monitors system connectivity and service availability.
Constraints: Ward medication access remains subject to local authorization, patient-care requirements, and applicable cabinet controls. Returned medication remains segregated from usable stock until disposition is assessed under hospital procedure. No explicit operating modes are defined."}
